answer: Bind each agent identity to one physical device through its quartz oscillator fingerprint. Every crystal drifts at a slightly different rate, so over hundreds of timed rounds the network measures a stable clock-skew signature no two chips share. An identity that cannot reproduce its measured skew is treated as hollow — a shell with no hardware behind it — and ejected from the shared garden of reputation, losing its staked history. Faking one fingerprint is cheap; faking ten thousand requires ten thousand real devices, turning a Sybil flood into a hardware bill of about $50 per identity.
